title: Delegated-Access Breach Investigation Playbook and Evidence Matrix
author: Marisol Vega
content:
Overview:
This playbook prescribes the investigation, evidence collection, and cross-team coordination steps for incidents involving delegated access or misuse of RBAC/authorization tokens. It covers triage, audit-log retrieval, chain-of-custody, data residency considerations, legal hold, and packaging of compliance evidence for audits and risk exceptions. The intent is to enable reproducible, forensically-sound investigations that meet regulatory and internal requirements while minimizing operational disruption.

Scope:
- Incident types: compromised service-account keys, delegated-role misuse, cross-tenant access attempts, token replay, mis-scoped IAM grants.
- Systems in scope: Control Plane (redwood-control), Authn/Authz service (redwood-auth), Audit pipeline (audit-ingest -> elasticsearch), Serving runtime gateway (inference-gateway), KMS/HSM integrations (kms-ext), Customer data stores (s3-regions, postgres-primary).
- Out of scope: physical data center breaches (escalate to ops), user-reported phishing unrelated to delegated tokens (handled by phishing-response guide).

Primary SLAs and Targets:
1) Initial triage: 1 hour from pager escalation.
2) Preliminary evidence package delivered to Legal/Security: 24 hours.
3) Full evidence bundle and incident timeline: 7 business days (complex cross-region cases may extend with approval).

Ownership and Roles:
- Incident Commander (IC): Security oncall lead — coordinates investigation and external comms.
- Forensics Lead: Security engineering — responsible for evidence capture and integrity.
- Auth Owner: Identity team — provides RBAC configuration and token validation logs.
- Infra/Logging Owner: Observability team — extracts audit pipeline artifacts and raw logs.
- Legal & Compliance: Provides legal hold guidance and external reporting cadence.
- Product/Customer Success: Customer-facing comms and contractual obligations.

Investigation Quick-Start Checklist (ordered):
1) Acknowledge and assign IC in PagerDuty; update incident channel.
2) Record metadata in Incident Tracker: incident_id, reporter, detection_time, affected_tenants, initial_scope.
3) Freeze change windows for affected services (temporary block deploys).
4) Capture triage snapshot (non-destructive):
   - Current RBAC policy versions (redwood-auth: /policies endpoint)
   - Active tokens list and last-used timestamps (redwood-auth DB view: active_tokens_vw)
   - Active sessions from inference-gateway (gateway/sessions API)
5) Begin evidence collection as described below.

Evidence Collection Matrix (what, why, retention & query examples):
| Evidence item | Why it matters | Minimum retention for IR | Example query (Elastic DSL / Splunk) | Responsible |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Authz decision logs (json) | Shows allow/deny, principal, resource, reason | 2 years for regulated customers; 1 year default | elastic: {"query":{"term":{"event_type":"authz_decision"}}} | Observability owner |
| Token issuance & revocation (kms-ext + redwood-auth) | Proof of credential lifecycle | 5 years if tied to audit request; 1 year default | splunk: index=auth token_action=issue OR token_action=revoke | Identity owner |
| API gateway access logs (ingress/egress) | Request path, headers (no PII), response codes | 1 year default; region-specific retention for data residency | elastic: {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"service":"inference-gateway"}}]}}} | Infra owner |
| KV cache access traces (serving runtime) | Detect replay or cache poisoning | 90 days | custom trace export from runtime-flush tool | Runtime team |
| Customer data read events (s3-regions) | Confirm exfiltration attempts | Per-customer contractual retention, legal hold overrides | s3 access logs prefix=customers/{tenant}/ | Storage owner |

Evidence Handling Rules:
- Always collect immutable copies: snapshot indices in Elastic (use _reindex to write to secure indices) and export raw logs to an encrypted evidence bucket in the same region as the data (e.g., evidence-us-east-1).
- Compute SHA256 checksum for each exported artifact and record in the chain-of-custody ledger (see template below).
- If evidence contains customer PII, flag and follow redaction guidance (reduce fields to tokenized IDs for investigators; full artifacts delivered only to Legal under NDA).
- Use KMS-wrapped envelopes when moving evidence between regions.

Chain-of-Custody Ledger Template (copy into secure docstore):
- incident_id: {INCIDENT_ID}
- artifact_id: {UUID}
- artifact_type: authz_decision | gateway_log | token_record | s3_access_log | config_snapshot
- created_by: {team_member}
- created_at: {UTC timestamp}
- checksum_sha256: {hex}
- storage_path: s3://evidence-bucket/{incident_id}/{artifact_id}.gz
- access_list: comma-separated list of user principals allowed to retrieve
- legal_hold_state: open | closed

Preservation Commands (examples):
- Elastic snapshot (preferred): curl -XPUT https://elastic-priv/_snapshot/ir-snap-1?wait_for_completion=true -d '{"indices":"authz-*,gateway-*","ignore_unavailable":true}'
- Export raw logs to evidence bucket: aws s3 cp /var/log/gateway/access.log s3://evidence-us-east-1/{incident_id}/gateway-access.log --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/evidence-key
- Token revocation (temporary block): POST https://redwood-auth.internal/v1/tokens/revoke {"token_id":"{token}"} (use admin key stored in vault)

Forensic Queries and Examples:
- Identify lateral movement via delegated roles:
  Elastic query: {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"event_type":"authn_success"}},{"term":{"auth.provider":"assume-role"}}],"filter":{"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-7d"}}}}}
- Token replay detection (gateway): count by token_id and distinct source IPs -> if count>1 and >3 distinct IPs in 4 hours, mark suspicious.

Data Residency & Cross-Region Rules:
- Always preserve evidence in the region where customer data resides unless Legal approves cross-border export. Evidence buckets are region-tagged (e.g. evidence-eu-west-1).
- When dealing with customers bound by residency constraints (e.g., EU personal data), restrict investigator access to staff with approved jurisdiction clearance.
- If a cross-border incident requires central analysis, use KMS-wrapped transfer and record justification in the incident timeline.

Interfacing with Secure SDLC and Post-Incident Remediation:
- If incident root cause traces to a code/infra change, attach the repro and blameable commit to the incident and trigger the secure-sdlc post-incident flow:
  1) Create a remediation PR with a security label and assign to authoring team.
  2) Run the security regression test suite (sec-ci) and the runtime perf smoke tests before canary.
  3) Enforce a canary rollout and monitor authz decision rates for 48 hours.
- Required artefacts for release: code diff, unit/integration/authorization tests, threat model update, deployment checklist signed off by Security.

Risk Exceptions and Compliance Evidence Packaging:
- If a remediation requires a temporary exception (e.g., relax token expiry to restore service), file a risk exception using the Risk Exception Form and attach the evidence package and compensating controls. Risk exceptions must include: owner, expiry date (max 90 days), mitigation plan, and monitoring metrics.
- Compliance evidence bundle checklist: incident timeline, preserved artifacts (with checksums), RBAC snapshots (pre/post), token revocation records, notification log (who was informed and when), legal hold statements.

Stakeholder Notification Matrix:
- T+0 (IC assigned): notify Security (pager), Observability, Identity, Legal.
- T+4h: product/customer-success if customers impacted. Draft customer-safe summary (no PII).
- T+24h: Legal & Finance for potential contractual/regulatory reporting.
- Regulatory triggers: follow jurisdiction-specific SLA for breach notification (e.g., GDPR 72-hour rule); Legal owns external filings.

Escalation and Decision Points:
- If evidence indicates confirmed data exfiltration of personal data, escalate to CTO and CEO within 4 hours.
- If evidence requires cross-border transfer to analyze, IC must document justification and obtain Legal approval prior to transfer.

Post-Incident Activities:
- Postmortem within 7 business days led by IC with action items tracked in the security backlog.
- Evidence retention review: mark artifacts for long-term retention or secure deletion per retention policy.
- Update RBAC policies, add automated alerts for the detected pattern, and schedule tabletop exercise covering the scenario.

Appendices:
A) Contact List (oncall rotation links): Security oncall -> https://pagerduty.com/redwood-security
B) Evidence Storage Naming Convention: evidence-{region}/{yyyy}/{incident_id}/{artifact_type}/{artifact_id}.gz
C) Frequently used CLI snippets and links:
   - Query authz decisions: curl -sS "https://kibana.internal/api/console/proxy?_path=_search" -H 'kbn-xsrf: true' -d '{"index":"authz-*","query":{"match_all":{}}}'
   - Revoke session tokens: ./tools/auth-revoke --token {token-id} --force --reason "ir:{incident_id}"

D) Change log: 2027-11-15 initial draft by Marisol Vega. 2028-02-10: expanded cross-region handling and added chain-of-custody template (reviewers: Aditya Rao, Claire Nguyen, Samir Patel).
